subject: Post-demo: Recommended model shortlist & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmepay.com>, Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@acmepay.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-demo: Recommended model shortlist & next steps

Hi Alex / Sophie —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. I wanted to recap our recommendations and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on evaluation priorities and timelines. Below is a short model shortlist tailored to Acme Payments’ requirements (transactional QA, structured extraction, and sub-200ms 512-token latency target for the live system). I’ve attached a small prompt set (acme_prompt_set_v1.csv) and our benchmark summary from today.

Recommended shortlist (tradeoffs: cost / latency / quality):

1) Redwood-Instruct-7B-q4 (recommended starter)
   - Rationale: Best balance of throughput and accuracy for structured extraction tasks. Runs well on 1x A10/A100; quantized q4 profiles give ~3–4x throughput improvement versus fp16 with minimal quality loss on extraction tests.
   - Expected latency: ~90–160ms for 512 tokens (batch=1, p99 on Dedicated).
   - Cost: Low-to-medium; good for high-volume endpoints where cost per token matters.

2) Mistral-Instruct-8B-16k (high-quality, medium-cost)
   - Rationale: Strong instruction-following and few-shot performance on complex parsing. Better at edge-case normalization and ambiguous instructions.
   - Expected latency: ~150–260ms for 512 tokens depending on hardware; consider batch tuning.
   - Cost: Medium; higher than Redwood-7B but often fewer tokens required due to better single-shot accuracy.

3) Llama2-13B-instruct (best-quality fallback)
   - Rationale: Highest raw quality on our generic NLU evals and more robust to prompt variability. Useful for canary/critical flows where precision is essential (e.g., dispute resolution).
   - Expected latency: ~220–400ms for 512 tokens on similar infra without aggressive quantization.
   - Cost: High; recommended as a fallback or for conservative rollouts.

Key notes / quality regression concerns:
- We recommend running your full prompt set (attached) + historical transaction samples to check regressions on structured fields (card BIN normalization, merchant names, 3DS flags).
- Quantization profiles (q4a/q4f) give strong cost/latency benefits but should be sanity-checked against the most sensitive keys — we can run a 24–48h eval and highlight deltas.
- If you need sub-100ms p95 for interactive flows, we should prioritize Redwood-Instruct-7B-q4 and dedicated A10 pools; otherwise Mistral-8B is a solid tradeoff.

Proposed next steps:
- Redwood: Run an internal eval (24–48h) across the attached prompt set + a 1k-sample historical set you provide. We’ll upload the results to the shared Drive link and flag any regressions.
- Technical sync: propose Tue/Wed next week for a 30–45 min session with Dev (SE) to review infra and perf targets.
- Trial access: we can enable sandbox credits and a limited Dedicated trial for performance tuning (requires a short SOW).

Attachments: acme_prompt_set_v1.csv, benchmark_summary_20260220.pdf

Cheers,

Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks for the concise summary, much appreciated. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Primary success metric: correctness of structured extraction (card last4, merchant normalization, MCC mapping). We’d like to see precision>98% on those fields in the eval.
- Latency: our target for customer-facing flows is p95 <200ms for 512 tokens. Background/async flows can tolerate higher latency.
- Budget: please provide a rough estimate for cost per 1M tokens for Redwood-Instruct-7B-q4 vs Mistral-8B so we can size the P&L.

We can share a 1k historical sample by EOD Monday. Also interested in a short Dedicated trial — let us know what you need from procurement.

Thanks,

Date: Sun, 22 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: technical notes on Acme shortlist (do not forward)

Team — quick technical notes to share before the Tues sync: 

1) Redwood-Instruct-7B-q4
   - Perf: on a single A10 (96GB) we see p95 ~110–150ms for 512 tokens with our q4 kernel; p99 closer to 200ms depending on infra noise. Memory footprint allows 3–4 concurrent instances per GPU depending on batch sizing.
   - Eval risk: q4 quantization occasionally trips up on subtle tokenization edge cases for merchant names (rare) — include normalization tests in the eval.
2) Mistral-Instruct-8B-16k
   - Perf: slightly higher memory; better zero-shot on entity disambiguation. p95 ~160–230ms on similar hardware.
   - Notes: recommend q4f quant profile for latency/cost tradeoff; verify floating point fallback for high-variance prompts.
3) Llama2-13B-instruct
   - Perf: will need fp16 or aggressive sharding for live p95 <300ms; not a primary candidate for interactive flows.

Eval plan (attached eval_plan_v1.md):
- Run 1k sample against each model + our house prompt set. Metrics: field-level precision/recall, normalized string edit distance for merchant names, and latency distribution (p50/p95/p99).
- Regression thresholds: fail if any critical field drops >1.5% in precision or average normalized edit distance increases >6% vs baseline.
- If regression observed on q4 models, we’ll run q4f/q5 fallback and report deltas.

Procurement note: to give them a Dedicated trial we’ll need a short SOW and a PO; Marissa can coordinate with Acme procurement.

— Dev
